_visibility_comment: PUBLIC from 2026-09-24, by Morgan's decision that day: "Make working-style
public too, go ahead." It joins precedent-shared-writing and
precedent-shared-repo-maintenance, both already public on GitHub. The point
is the next step: a public repo may then carry this set's text in its
tracked tree, so a session whose clones fail at start still has it.
DECLARED BEFORE THE GITHUB SETTING FLIPS, deliberately. Declared public
while actually private is the safe direction -- the leak gate scans more,
nothing is published. The other order is the one that bit
Checked before flipping: the leak gate over the tracked tree, and every
commit in history against the same blocklist and an email pattern. The
only hits were a fixture identity in tools/checks/tests/test_assorted_notes.sh,
replaced with a placeholder in the same commit. That address was already
public anyway, as the author of every commit in the two public sets.
The original note, still why this key is declared outright:
build_views.repo_is_public() reads an ABSENT precedent.json as private --
no config, not a Precedent repo -- but a PRESENT one with no 'visibility'
key as PUBLIC. Omitting it is how a repo gets the wrong answer silently.
_fallback_timezone_comment: The zone for stamping commits and generated dates in THIS repo when
nobody's own zone resolves -- no PRECEDENT_COMMIT_TZ, no identity.json
reachable, no TZ in the environment. It is rung 5 of the ladder in
tools/precedent_time.py: a person's zone is person-level and lives in
their identity.json, while the answer for a person this project could
not identify is the repository's to choose.

New York, not Buenos Aires. This is a TEAM set: shared by level, and consumed by repositories with more than one member. Buenos Aires is Morgan's own zone and belongs in his individual source, not in a set an unidentified committer could be anyone in. Morgan, 2026-09-10: the Buenos Aires fallback is just for him personally; a shared set defaults to New York. Sibling declarations the same day: precedent-team-repo-maintenance, precedent-team-writing, and the nomen-omen consuming repo.
APPLIED, NEVER ENFORCED, exactly as the engine-level rung below it is.
Applied, because the alternative is not 'no zone' but the container's
silent UTC, and a record stamped +0000 by somebody who is not in UTC
cannot be ordered against anyone else's. Never enforced, because
refusing somebody's commit over a zone THEY never declared blocks real
work on a value they never saw. Declaring a zone in your own
identity.json is what makes it yours and checked.

_commit_author_check_comment: check_commit_author.py was vendored into this repo (tools/checks/,
practices/) on 2026-09-19. precedent-individual is deliberately NOT
added to the `sources` list above -- build_views refuses that
outright: naming an individual source in a shared repo's tracked
config would leak its existence and location to anyone who reads the
repo. Identity resolves correctly anyway, via the untracked
~/.config/precedent/config.json, a mechanism entirely separate from
this file's `sources` (which is only for practice TEXT reaching this
repo's generated views).
check_buenos_aires_dates.py and practices/buenos-aires-dates.md were
vendored alongside it in that same 2026-09-19 pass and reverted the
same day: the fallback_timezone comment above already established,
nine days earlier, that Buenos Aires is Morgan's own zone and belongs
in his individual source, not in a set an unidentified committer
could be anyone in -- the vendoring pass copied the practice FILE
because its check script is mechanically generic (identity.json-
keyed, same shape as commit-author's), without checking whether the
practice's own prose was written for a shared audience. It was not:
the file opens 'It's my own timezone'. Landing byte-identically in
all three team sets left `buenos-aires-dates` a same-level tie no
resolver could break the moment a consumer (precedent-individual)
declared more than one of them as a source -- caught the same day it
landed, when precedent_sync_views.py refused for exactly that reason.
commit-author.md stays: its own text says the mechanism is generic
and meant to be copied into other people's individual sets, which a
shared team repo declaring it satisfies without contradiction.
Of the 11 grandfathered SHAs this pass originally added, the 8 whose
note said the commit was correctly-authored and tripped only
check_buenos_aires_dates.py were removed with it below -- nothing
left to exempt once that check is gone. The 3 that also trip (or
trip only) check_commit_author.py stay.
